transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you’re here. What brings you in today?

Hello, Doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me. I, um... I hope I'm doing this right. I don't want to sound like a complainer, because I really do try to get along with everyone, but... well, I'm here because for nearly two years now, I’ve just been so sure that our contractor and... and some of the people on my block have been quietly working together. 

It's a little embarrassing to even say out loud, and I don't want you to think poorly of me, but I really believe they're trying to cheat us. They're keeping my kitchen half-wrong on purpose. My husband, bless his heart, he keeps showing me all the receipts and repeating all the excuses they give him, but... I just know what's happening. 

Does... does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining things the way you need me to.
Have you been hearing or seeing things that other people around you do not?

Oh, goodness, no. No, nothing like that. I... I would tell you if I did, I promise. I don't hear voices or see anything that isn't really there. I know sometimes people who come to see a psychiatrist might struggle with those kinds of things, but... well, for me, it's really just the situation with the contractor and the kitchen. It's all just... ordinary things that are happening, right out in the open. 

I hope that's an okay answer? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information, doctor.
Have you ever been able to doubt that this might not be true?

I... well, I try to. I really do. I don't want to be a difficult person, and I hate the idea of accusing anyone of something awful. Sometimes I sit down and I look at the receipts my husband brings me, and I listen to the excuses the contractor gives him about supply chain issues or wrong measurements... and I try so hard to just accept it. 

But... oh, I hope this doesn't make me sound stubborn, but no matter how much I try to doubt it, I just can't. It's been nearly two years, and the kitchen is still half-wrong, and I just... I know they're working together to cheat us. The contractor and those neighbors. I just know it in my bones, even when I try to talk myself out of it. 

Is it... is it bad that I can't let it go? I really am trying my best to see it from another side, doctor.
Has this belief affected other parts of your life in the same way, or is it only about the contractor and the kitchen?

Oh, no, it's really just the kitchen. I hope that's a relief to hear? I don't want you to think my whole life is in shambles or that I'm falling apart, because I'm really not. 

Outside of dealing with the remodel and... and the contractor, everything else is just fine. I still keep up with my church gatherings every week, and my book club... I wouldn't miss those for the world. I do all my usual household routines, and my husband and I still make all our regular family plans. I'm still me, you know? Just... dealing with this one very frustrating thing. 

Does that sound normal to you? I just want to reassure you that I'm keeping everything else together just fine.
Do you think there is any chance at all that the contractor and your neighbors are actually working together to cheat you?

Oh... well, yes. I... I don't want to sound like a difficult woman, but it's more than just a chance. Honestly, it's the whole reason I'm here to see you. 

For nearly two years now, I’ve been absolutely sure that the contractor and some of the people on my block have been quietly working together to cheat us. They are keeping my kitchen half-wrong on purpose. I know I mentioned it a moment ago, but... well, no matter how many receipts my husband shows me, or how many excuses they give, I just know they're doing it. 

I hope you don't think I'm being unreasonable or paranoid by saying that. I know it's not a very nice thing to accuse people of, but I just want to be completely honest with you so you have all the facts. Am I explaining it okay? I want to make sure I'm answering your questions properly.
How certain are you that this belief is true, even if someone else thinks it sounds unlikely?

I... well, I hope this doesn't make you think less of me, but I'm completely certain. I know it might sound strange to someone else, and I really wish it wasn't happening, but I just know it's true. 

It's... it's like I said before, I'm really only here because of this whole situation. For almost two years, I've just been so sure that the contractor and those people on my street are... well, that they're working together behind our backs. To cheat us, and to make sure my kitchen stays in this awful, half-finished state on purpose. 

I know my husband tries to show me the receipts, and the contractor always has some excuse ready, but... I just know what's really going on, even if it's hard for others to see. I'm sorry if that sounds very stubborn of me. I really don't want to be a difficult patient. Does that make sense, doctor? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right answers.
Aside from the contractor and the kitchen, do you have any other beliefs that you’re equally certain are true but that other people say are untrue?

Oh, no... no, definitely not. I really hope that puts your mind at ease? I know this whole kitchen business must sound... well, a bit much to you, and I'd hate for you to think I'm just making things up all over the place. 

But I promise, I don't go around thinking people are out to get me in general. It's truly just this one specific situation with the remodel. Everything else in my life is completely normal, I assure you. I don't have any other... strange ideas, or whatever people might call them. 

I try to be very reasonable about everything else in my life. Does that help answer your question? I really don't want you to worry that I'm losing touch with reality or anything like that. I'm just a regular person dealing with a very bad contractor.
